  addScriptTag: function addScriptTag(options = {}, prependToBody = false) {
  const script = document.createElement('script');

  const opts = {
    language: 'javascript',
    type: 'text/javascript',
    ...options
  };

  Object.keys(opts).forEach((key) => {
    if (key === 'data') {
      const { data } = opts;
      Object.keys(data).forEach((dataKey) => {
        if (data[dataKey]) {
          script.setAttribute(`data-${dataKey}`, data[dataKey]);

      window.CNN.Zion.environmentType &&
      window.CNN.Zion.sourceId &&
      window.ZION_SDK

      const environment = window.ZION_SDK.EnvironmentType[window.CNN.Zion.environmentType];
      const enableLogging = environment !== window.ZION_SDK.EnvironmentType.Prod;

      if (window.zion_analytics) {
        window.addEventListener('zionReady', (evt) => {
          window.zion_analytics.track(new window.ZION_SDK.Pageview({
            canonicalUrl: window.CNN.contentModel.canonicalUrl,
            traits: {
              event_source: window.CNN.contentModel.techStack || 'stellar',
              page_variant: window.CNN.contentModel.templateType || '',
              raw_url: window.location.href,
              cms_id: CNN.contentModel.cmsId || '',
              page_type: CNN.contentModel.pageType || '',
              edition: window.CNN.helpers.isEditionPage(),
              section: CNN.contentModel.section || '',
              subsection: CNN.contentModel.subsection || '',

              experience_type: 'cnn_core',
              page_tags: window.CNN.metadata.content.topics.tags || window.CNN.contentModel.pageTags.split(',')

            sourceId: window.CNN.contentModel.sourceId || ''

            consent_state: window.WBD.UserConsent.getSimpleConsentState() || {}
          }));
        }, {once: true});

        window.zion_analytics.configure({
          bridgeEnabled: true,
          bufferSize: 20,
          enableLogging,
          customFeatureManagerPath: 'https://z.cdp-dev.cnn.com/zfm/zfh-3.js',
          environment: window.CNN.Zion.environmentType,
          isSecure: true,
          telemetryEndpoint: window.env.ZION_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT,
          trackAdvertising: false,
          trackBluetooth: false,
          trackDeeplink: false,
          trackLifecycle: false,
          trackLocation: false,
          trackNotifications: false,
          trackPurchases: false,
          trackScreens: false,
          trackUxMetrics: true,
          uxMetricsPercentage: 15
        });
      } else {
        console.error('zion: "zion_analytics" failed to load properly.');
      }
    } else {
      throw new Error('zion: missing either "apiKey", "environmentType" or "sourceId"');
    }
  });
})();

        <script>
          (function() {
            function getPath() {
                const domain = window.location.hostname;
                const metaURL = document.querySelector('[rel=canonical]').getAttribute?.('href');
                try {
                    const canURL = new URL(metaURL);
                    return domain + canURL.pathname;
                } catch (e) {
                    // we should never run into this situation where the canonical
                    // url is missing in the meta tag but just in case
                    return domain + document.location.pathname;
                }
            }
            function getDomain() {
              var domain = 'cnn.com';
              if (window.CNN.helpers.isEspanolPage()) {
                domain = 'cnnespanol.cnn.com';
              } else if (window.CNN.helpers.isArabicPage()) {
                domain = 'arabic.cnn.com';
              } else if (window.CNN.helpers.isEditionPage()) {
                domain = 'edition.cnn.com';
              }
              if (window.CNN.omniture.rs_flag != "prod") {
                domain = "dev." + domain;
              }
              return domain;
            }
            function getTitle(headline = '') {
              const isHomepage = window.CNN?.contentModel?.section === 'homepage';
              return isHomepage ? headline.replace(' Desktop', '').replace(' Mobile', '') : headline;
            }
            const isWebview = window.location.pathname.startsWith('/webview');
            var _sf_async_config = window._sf_async_config = (window._sf_async_config || {});
            _sf_async_config.uid = 37612;
            _sf_async_config.domain = getDomain();
            _sf_async_config.sections = window.CNN.contentModel.vertical;
            _sf_async_config.authors = window.CNN.omniture.cap_author;
            _sf_async_config.title = getTitle(window.CNN.omniture.headline);
            _sf_async_config.flickerControl = false;
            _sf_async_config.path = getPath();
            if(isWebview) {
                _sf_async_config.mobileApp = true;
            }
          })();

After all, there are so many new product releases that it’s hard to know what’s worth caring about, let alone worth buying. That’s why we rounded up a short list of our favorites from the last seven days. This week, I take a hands-on look at the Lego Smart Play Pokémon sets, recap filming a beach trip with the new Insta360 Luna Pro camera and look into how the recent Fitbit Air is channeling Pikachu to help you get a better night sleep. All that and more in this week’s coverage. Lego Smart Play Pokémon Sets A hands-on look after a building them myself and chatting with the designers It’s been a month since Lego released its second wave of Smart Play sets as part of its Pokémon collection. Since then, I’ve built many of the sets for myself after buying them alongside other Lego launches in August. I even had the chance to speak with two of the masterminds behind the Smart Brick at the Pokémon World Championships in San Francisco, California. With the holiday season around the corner and Lego gifts primed to be more popular than ever, I’m circling back on the new interactive kits to see how they stack up. This is by no means a full review, but I am so impressed by how night and day the difference is between the original Star Wars kits from back in March, and these new Pokémon sets. The very nature of augmenting Pokémon made out of bricks lends itself far better to interactive play with the Smart Brick than adding lights and sounds to an X-Wing ever could. At least for me. On their own, the sets are still cute little creations true to the source material, and when paired with the Smart Brick, the Pokémon can do everything from battle like in the games with typing advantages and charged attacks to leveling up, interacting with each other via adorable growls and using sound effects to imitate swimming, flying or crawling. Part of that difference in experiences starts from the people behind the scenes. I had a chance to speak with a pair of Lego Designers, Siddharth Muthyala and Mike Andersen, in order to hear more about what it meant to bring Pokémon to life. It was clear right after building the kits that there was something special about these video game characters compared to the starfighters from a galaxy far, far away, and I’ve been dying to know just why that was the case. Time seems to be one of the largest factors. Andersen, the Senior Design Manager at Lego, notes that his first day on the job was spent figuring out how to accurately portray Pokémon in the blocky medium. He spent the better part of four years — well before Lego announced that it had acquired the license to Pokémon — working on designing hundreds of different characters from the franchise as part of a team that was entirely separate from the Lego Star Wars designers. With the help of Muthyala, the company’s Design Director, Lego was able to release sets that I’ve found to be incredibly fun. Lego Pokémon Charizard vs. Jolteon Ultimate Battle  One of the only complete kits that includes the actual Lego Smart Brick, this set comes with the fan-favorite Charizard alongside Jolteon and two of the interactive bricks. After building it for myself, I found this to be one of the better introductions to what Lego Smart Play has to offer. Lego Pokémon Mewtwo's Lab Break  This is one of the Lego sets I bought back in August, and it is easily my favorite of the batch. Even though it is part of the Smart Play line, it still looks great as a display model with a solid build for Mewtwo as well as lab equipment inspired by the first Pokémon film. Lego Pokémon Eevee and Lapras's Treasure Hunt  Lego may have already released a larger version of Eevee as part of its first wave of Pokémon sets from earlier in the year, but it had to include the beloved character as part of its Smart Play line. I adore this set, especially with how great Eevee and Lapras look in their blocky, Lego designs. Lego Pokémon Trainer's Buggy Adventure With Squirtle  This set from Lego's Pokémon collection takes a more playful approach to the source material. Does Squirtle drive a car in any of the video games? Nope. Is this set still awesome? Of course it is — they're driving a beach buggy! In my conversation, they also teased the future of the Smart Brick and Lego Pokémon as a whole. At Pokémon Worlds, Lego gave fans an early look at some of the pocket monsters that will be getting the brick-built treatment in 2027, revealing silhouettes of Grookey, Pichu, Mankey, Wingull and Charcadet. Beyond just which models builders will be able to piece together in the future, I had to ask about what’s to come from the Smart Brick. As of now, Lego Pokémon only have a set amount of ways to interact with each other. But it may not be like that for long. Muthyala, with a large grin on his face, said he really wanted to share what was in the works, but couldn’t just yet. Andersen, on the other hand, provided some concrete insight into the future: So while we have a confirmation that there’s more to come from the actual sets in the Lego Smart Play collection, we’ll have to wait and see what the interactive elements of those builds look like. Back when I took a hands-on look at the Star Wars Smart Play sets, it felt like they weren’t fully taking advantage of the impressive technology inside of the Smart Brick. My time with the Pokémon sets is such a step forward in unlocking the full potential, and both Muthyala and Anderson seem excited to continue driving that forward. Lego Pokémon Smart Play sets are now available for purchase directly from Lego’s online storefront as well as other retailers like Amazon. Insta360 Luna Pro The first gimbal camera with 4K vertical recording Insta360 just launched its newest gimbal camera, the Luna Pro. Despite costing less than the Luna Ultra that I’ve been using over the past few months, this is hardly a downgrade. In fact, it upgrades one key feature that even the higher-end version lacks; the ability to record 4K vertical video. Typically with these gimbal cameras, whether from Insta360 or DJI or some other brand, you’re limited to filming vertical content at 3K. Some of these video cameras are able to capture the world around you with an 8K resolution in landscape orientation. But when you want to record footage fit for sharing on Instagram or the social media platform of your choice? It’s locked to a lower quality. That’s no longer the case thanks to the debut of the Insta360 Luna Pro. Instead of hiding this feature behind a higher-end version, Insta360 has decided to release a more affordable iteration that improves one of the biggest use cases for this type of camera while making some sacrifices in other, less used areas. Filming 4K content in a portrait orientation will be rolling out to the Luna Ultra in the near future, but for now, it’s nice to see the cheaper model debut with such a highly sought-after feature. Aside from its vertical video capabilities, the biggest difference between the new Luna Pro and the Luna Ultra that came before it is the lack of a secondary sensor. The latter has a telephoto zoom lens that helps with taking videos of far away subjects, and for this new and more affordable version, Insta360 has ditched that feature. In my own personal testing, I haven’t found myself using the extra zoom capabilities all that much and certainly agree that it’s worth nixing from the experience in favor of saving nearly $200. Aside from the different camera array that rests on the gimbal, the Insta360 Luna Pro is every bit the same that I’ve been relying on for the past few months. It still includes the detachable screen and control pad that’s every bit as innovative on the new release as they are on the Ultra version. It still has solid battery life that can easily record clips throughout an entire day of on-and-off shooting. It still uses Leica color science for cinematic shots right out of the camera. And most importantly, its gimbal stabilization ensures that shaky videos are a thing of the past, even when you’re being nudged by waves while at the beach. All of that makes the lower $600 price tag such a bargain in my book. Most casual videographers won’t miss any of the exclusive features that are only found on the Luna Ultra, especially with it landing at $170 below that higher-end version of the gimbal camera. Fitbit Air Pokémon Sleep Special Edition Catch some Zzz’s and some pocket monsters with Pokémon Sleep integration Whoop is the king of screen-free fitness trackers. If you want a device that tracks your steps, heart rate and sleep without having to deal with a full smartwatch, Whoop truly is the device to dethrone. Earlier this year, the new Fitbit Air launched with a robust suite of health-tracking tech to help it take on such a worthy adversary, and now, it’s getting some extra help from an unlikely ally: Pikachu. The new Pokémon Sleep edition of the Fitbit Air is every bit the same health monitor that that my colleague and CNN Underscored’s senior testing editor, Rick Stella, tried for himself back in June. It still handles keeping tabs on your well-being, works for up to seven days before needing to be recharged, can tag along in the shower and even while swimming with water-resistance that is rated to withstand depths of up to 50 meters. It just has a fun new design that complements some added software tricks that allow the Fitbit Air to work with the smartphone app, Pokémon Sleep. Normally, you need to pay for a Google Health subscription in order to unlock deeper insight into your sleep routine and workout regimen. While Pokémon Sleep can’t help with the latter, it does unlock all kinds of info on how long and how well you sleep at night. It also adds some extra encouragement to getting to bed on time, with a simply delightful experience that turns catching some Zzz’s into catching Pokémon. During my time at the Pokémon World Championships, I also had a chance to check out the new wearable and put it to the test alongside the Pokémon Sleep app that I’ve used intermittently over the years. The Fitbit Air itself is such a simple yet great piece of hardware that truly lives up to the notion that you can just set it and forget it on your wrist. I may not be ditching my beloved Apple Watch anytime soon, but I do envy just how convenient it is to wear this screen-free fitness tracker. The newfound compatibility with the Pocket Monster-themed application is also a delight, and is a perfect match for the themed accessory. I can’t help being a bit biased that the Fitbit Air’s nylon strap has received a makeover to my favorite color, blue, and the little Pikachu insignia is just such a cute addition. The Pokémon Sleep Special Edition of Fitbit Air is now available for purchase directly from Google and retails for $130, which is the same price as the other unique editions of the wearable. It begins shipping next week on Sept. 15. Nomad iPhone 18 Cases My favorite cases were just updated for Apple’s latest devices Apple’s new iPhone 18 smartphones were revealed this week, and that means a slew of new ways to protect and accessorize your device. But if there’s just one brand worth highlighting first, it’s the latest collection of covers from Nomad. The brand is a longtime favorite amongst many of CNN Underscored’s editors, and has been protecting my personal smartphones for nearly a decade now. Getting my hands on whatever new case Nomad puts out each fall to go alongside Apple’s fresh smartphones is practically a ritual at this point, and there are even more options to choose from for 2026. On top of new iterations of cases the company has been making for years, Nomad has taken the iPhone 18 Pro series launch as a chance to introduce some entirely new designs into its portfolio. There’s still the same affinity for using some of the best leather that you’ll find in a smartphone case, as well as more rugged offerings and even the brand’s first clear case in recent memory. I’ve gone on record time and time again to deem this my favorite leather cover for the better part of a decade, and the newest iteration remains largely unchanged. Sure, there are some new tweaks to adapt to the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max’s adjusted designs, but otherwise, you’re still looking at a choice between either Horween or Nomad’s standard leather. Alongside its new iPhone 18 Pro series cases, Nomad is has also released some covers for the iPhone Duo. There aren’t as many styles to choose from compared to the more typical candy bar-style devices, but just having the option to cover Apple’s first folding smartphone in a leather suit of amor is more than enough for the first wave of releases. Nomad’s Traditional Leather Folio has long been my preferred way to carry an ID and credit cards alongside my iPhone, and it’s even more of a perfect fit for the iPhone Duo’a passport-inspired build. There’s also a fresh take on the company’s unique magnetic leather cover that will help protect the back panel of the folding phone without as much extra padding around its titanium frame and exterior display. Each of the new Nomad cases is now available for purchase. The standard iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max covers will begin shipping right alongside their respective smartphones next week, while the iPhone Duo accessories will be similarly coming out around the same time as their device. The Duo won’t be shipping until October, and Nomad will be following suit by releasing its leather cases for the smartphone in November. Suri Core Sonic Electric Toothbrush Teeth-cleaning with plant-based brush heads Suri has impressed CNN Underscored editors with its sustainable electric toothbrushes that don’t compromise on brushing quality just because its brush heads are made from a cornstarch material. One of the biggest issues with these types of toothbrushes are the fact that their replacement brushes end up creating waste, which Suri has been helping solve with its plant-based construction. It just released its newest version of the sustainable toothbrush that arrives with many of the same bells and whistles as the version our team reviewed, just with a lower price tag. The new Suri Core is $25 less than the original model, while still delivering four weeks of battery life that makes it a perfect traveling companion, a pressure sensor to prevent over-brushing and sonic cleaning vibrations. I’ve been trying out the Suri Core for myself over the past few weeks, and was even able to put it to the test on a recent vacation. I haven’t had to charge it since I first removed it from the package, which certainly validates that the Core is every bit as reliable as the travel toothbrush that my colleague and our travel editor Kyle Olsen relies on. The Suri Core Sonic Electric Toothbrush is now available for purchase for $75. You can pick it up on Amazon in you choice of four new shades: Haze Green, Ember Orange, Nightfall Blue and Moonrise Gray. Philips OneUp 5000 A premium cordless electric mop with a lightweight design There’s a new contender for the best high-end mop, and it’s not from the usual suspects. Sure, Philips is no stranger to reliable appliances and gadgets that clean everything from floors to teeth, but its newest electric mop, the OneUp 5000, takes that up a notch with a far more premium experience than the affordable options our editors typically recommend all at a fraction of the cost of other comparable solutions from Dyson, iRobot or Roborock. The Philips OneUp 5000 rests somewhere between those feature-packed options and traditional mops like models from O-Cedar or Swiffer. Unlike the latter which keep clean by spreading dirty water around or relying on some kind of extra cleaning solution, the OneUp continuously pumps clean water onto your floor while simultaneously sucking in dirty water into a separate tank. It’s still quite the lightweight appliance, too, despite a pair of onboard water tanks and a rechargeable battery that powers the mopping experience for up to 70 minutes on a single charge. One of my favorite elements about the mop is that you won’t have to worry about wasting single-use cleaning pads that you’ll have to repurchase every few months. Instead, the OneUp relies on a reusable, machine-washable pad to do the job. At $230, the latest mop from Philips has an impressive lineup of features that makes it more capable than the cheaper mops CNN Underscored typically recommends, without the added bulk or price from the higher-end options out there. I’ll be excited to see how my colleagues view its combination of value and cleaning capabilities once they inevitably get their hands on one, but for now, you can try it out for yourself by purchasing it directly from Philips. Nintendo Direct Recap Preorder the latest games for Nintendo Switch 2 This week, Nintendo also held its latest Direct online showcase to preview the future of its Switch 2 console. Alongside an early look at the upcoming release of Kirby and the World Beyond ahead of hitting consoles for Kirby’s 35th anniversary in 2027, Nintendo also put several new titles up for preorder. All the stars like Samus, Link and Captain Olimar have made the cut with the latest side-scrolling Metroid adventure, a remake for one of the classic The Legend of Zelda games and an improved Switch 2 version of Pikmin 4 with bonus content. Below, you’ll get a full rundown of four of the new announcements. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time  Ocarina of Time has been ported over to the Switch 2 with a giant leap in graphical fidelity. It's one of the most iconic games in all of Nintendo history, and now fans who have been enjoying it for the past 28 years can replay it on their modern handheld, while newer gamers will finally get to see why the Water Temple level is as infamous as it is. The Legend of Zelda remake launches later this fall on Nov. 5. Metroid Ravenous  The last side-scrolling, adventure game from the Metroid series, Metroid Dread, launched a few years back. It's been one of my favorite titles on the Switch since I first agonized over its complex map and challenging levels. This week, Nintendo announced it'll be doubling down with a sequel. Metroid Ravenous launches on Jan. 28 next year exclusively on the Switch 2 and gives players far more ways to control the renowned bounty hunter, Samus Aran. Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy  I'm one of the biggest Pikmin fans around. So while getting an enhanced version of the latest game designed to run on the new Switch 2 isn't the most exciting reveal from this week's Nintendo Direct, it may be the announcement I'm most looking forward to actually playing. On top of improvements to match the more powerful console, Pikmin 4 also comes with a new Dandori Academy battle mode when it launches on Nov. 12. Pokémon Pokopia Expansion Pass Bundle  Pokémon just released the first part of the Pokopia Expansion Pass with the Bubbly Basin area, and now, we've received a look at the second wave of additional content. In Part 2, you'll be able to dress up Ditto and other Pokémon in a range of adorable accessories like sunglasses, bow ties and even items inspired by other Pokémon like a Sylveon ribbon! BenQ Inftylab M Wireless Mouse A lightweight take on an ergonomic mouse I may be one of the biggest laptop trackpad fans around, but even I can’t ignore the siren song of a comfortable, ergonomic mouse. I’ve tried dozens over the years, and sadly, I almost always go back to using my trusty Apple Magic Trackpad. That streak was finally broken by the recent Logitech MX Master 4, a computer accessory that currently holds CNN Underscored’s title for the best mouse we’ve tested. As much as I enjoy how comfortable it is to use for hours on end, it largely only ever lives on my desk. That’s all well and good for the days when I work in my home office, but if I find myself working by the window in my cozy lounge chair or even heading out to work at a coffee shop, I simply go back to using the trackpad built right into my laptop. That’s where the new BenQ Inftylab M comes into play. It’s one of the first ergonomic mice on the market that is designed specifically for Mac gestures, taking a more focused approach than the universal Mac and Windows compatibility that you’ll find from Logitech. Compared to the MX Master 4, the M Mouse is just shy of half its weight at just 85 grams. That’s really where BenQ’s newest mouse catches my attention. It may not cradle my hand in quite the same way as Logitech’s much larger and heavier peripheral, but the Inftylab M still feels great to use after a day of clicking and scrolling. Being able to bring the trackpad experience with me without wasting precious space in my backpack makes for an easy selling point, although the $100 price tag for this new mouse does make it a tougher comparison. I’ll be excited to spend more time with the Inftylab mouse to see how it compares in the long run, but so far, I’m impressed by its ability to replicate trackpad and Multi-Touch gestures with its shortcut buttons on the side. Paired with its lightweight and ergonomic design, this is certainly a winning combination — especially if the larger Logitech MX options just aren’t as comfortable for those with smaller hands or practical to use while away from your home office. The BenQ Inftylab M Wireless Mouse is now available for preorder at retailers like B&H Photo Video for $100. Moment iPhone 18 Cases These colorful covers improve your iPhone’s photography This year’s newest iPhones make even bigger strides in turning your smartphone into a reliable camera. Moment has been helping photographers make the switch to the handset they already have in their pocket by making some of the best accessories to help double down on that sentiment. For the iPhone 18 Pro series devices, there’s a new line of cases tailored to the latest hardware changes. Available in five colors, the new covers wrap your smartphone in a grippy exterior that helps improve how easy it is to hold while shooting photos while also adding some extra protection with a rubber bumper around the edges. Aside from the practicality of these Moment iPhone cases, the real star of the show is the bundled SmartAlign Lens Mount. It allows you to snap on any of Moment’s T-Series mobile lenses in order to augment the already incredible cameras that come attached to the back of Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max. The cases are also made to work with the company’s QuickLock filters, which allow you to add press-and-lock filters over the built-in camera module for getting more professional results. Moment’s latest cases are now available for purchase. Like previous editions, each one sells for $55 and comes in designs meant to complement the new colors that Apple has introduced for its latest smartphones. You’ll also find a complete suite of photography accessories for the iPhone 18 Pro series on Moment’s site, including specialized MagSafe mounts, the previously mentioned mobile lenses and more versatile film cages. Arc Pulse iPhone 18 Pro Cases These eye-catching aluminum bumper cases are back Last up on the docket of new iPhone 18 cases are the latest covers from Arc. The brand takes a vastly different approach to protecting your new smartphone compared to any other accessories covered this week. That’s thanks to an aluminum build that aims to offer the most protection possible while also covering as little of your smartphone as it can. Each bumper case is made from two individual pieces of aluminum, which pair with rubber padding to protect the top and bottom corners of your handset. Arc Pulse cases lift your smartphone off a desk, so laying it down doesn’t scuff or scratch the screen. I have been a massive fan of these Arc bumper cases for years. There have been entire years where the only case I actually use with my annual iPhone upgrade is one of these Arc covers, and every time, I am always left impressed by how well something so minimal can actually protect my device. So, if you’re worried that these minimal covers don’t provide enough protection, hopefully my anecdotal experience with the accessory should help put your mind at ease. Alongside the refreshed designs fit for Apple’s newest Pro series smartphones (the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max), Arc is also shipping in six styles: Matte Black, Silver, Graphite, Rose Bronze, Gold and Titanium Onyx Black. Pricing across the new collection starts at $70.                     <p

            Every Friday, our deals experts set aside their usual affinities for finding discounts to search the web for the week’s <a href="https://www.cnn.com/cnn-underscored/reviews/product-news">best product drops</a>. After all, there are so many new product releases that it’s hard to know what’s worth caring about, let alone worth buying. That’s why we rounded up a short list of our favorites from the last seven days.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtn7t5fj007g27qh50uqh0kw@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            This week, I take a hands-on look at the <a href="https://www.amazon.com/stores/page/1D1AD182-431E-4D34-9B76-749EBBB2B1CF?ingress=2&lp_context_asin=B0G2T1NQMW&visitId=64aa4366-22fd-4c43-846a-40758cff07cc&store_ref=bl_ast_dp_brandlogo_sto&ref_=ast_bln&tag=Underscoreddefault-20&ascsubtag=091126productlaunches" rel="nofollow sponsored" target="_blank">Lego Smart Play Pokémon sets</a>, recap filming a beach trip with the new <a href="https://www.amazon.com/Insta360-CINSACHA-Luna-Vlogging-Camera/dp/B0GY87RFYK?tag=Underscoreddefault-20&ascsubtag=091126productlaunches" rel="nofollow sponsored" target="_blank">Insta360 Luna Pro</a> camera and look into how the recent <a href="https://go.skimresources.com/?id=87732X1565017&url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.google.com%2Fconfig%2Fgoogle_fitbit_air%3Fhl%3Den-US%26selections%3DeyJwcm9kdWN0RmFtaWx5IjoiWjI5dloyeGxYMlpwZEdKcGRGOWhhWEk9IiwidmFyaWFudHMiOltbIjciLCJNVEk9Il0sWyIyIiwiT0E9PSJdXX0%253D&xcust=091126productlaunches" rel="nofollow sponsored" target="_blank">Fitbit Air</a> is channeling Pikachu to help you get a better night sleep. All that and more in this week’s coverage.
    </p>

        A hands-on look after a building them myself and chatting with the designers
</h3>

<div

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtwzkk6h00er3b662bqrkm3i@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            It’s been a month since Lego released its <a href="https://www.amazon.com/stores/page/1D1AD182-431E-4D34-9B76-749EBBB2B1CF?ingress=2&lp_context_asin=B0G2T1NQMW&visitId=64aa4366-22fd-4c43-846a-40758cff07cc&store_ref=bl_ast_dp_brandlogo_sto&ref_=ast_bln&tag=Underscoreddefault-20&ascsubtag=091126productlaunches" rel="nofollow sponsored" target="_blank">second wave of Smart Play sets</a> as part of its Pokémon collection. Since then, I’ve built many of the sets for myself after buying them alongside other Lego launches in August. I even had the chance to speak with two of the masterminds behind the Smart Brick at the Pokémon World Championships in San Francisco, California. With the holiday season around the corner and Lego gifts primed to be more popular than ever, I’m circling back on the new interactive kits to see how they stack up.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtwzrfyj00f73b66l8b9yynp@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            This is by no means a full review, but I am so impressed by how night and day the difference is between the original Star Wars kits from back in March, and these new Pokémon sets. The very nature of augmenting Pokémon made out of bricks lends itself far better to interactive play with the Smart Brick than adding lights and sounds to an X-Wing ever could. At least for me. On their own, the sets are still cute little creations true to the source material, and when paired with the Smart Brick, the Pokémon can do everything from battle like in the games with typing advantages and charged attacks to leveling up, interacting with each other via adorable growls and using sound effects to imitate swimming, flying or crawling.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtx0k07800hd3b66pi477sog@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            Part of that difference in experiences starts from the people behind the scenes. I had a chance to speak with a pair of Lego Designers, Siddharth Muthyala and Mike Andersen, in order to hear more about what it meant to bring Pokémon to life. It was clear right after building the kits that there was something special about these video game characters compared to the starfighters from a galaxy far, far away, and I’ve been dying to know just why that was the case. Time seems to be one of the largest factors. Andersen, the Senior Design Manager at Lego, notes that his first day on the job was spent figuring out how to accurately portray Pokémon in the blocky medium. He spent the better part of four years — well before Lego announced that it had acquired the license to Pokémon — working on designing hundreds of different characters from the franchise as part of a team that was entirely separate from the Lego Star Wars designers. With the help of Muthyala, the company’s Design Director, Lego was able to release sets that I’ve found to be incredibly fun.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtwzz59u00fe3b66dyh4hxz7@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            In my conversation, they also teased the future of the Smart Brick and Lego Pokémon as a whole. At Pokémon Worlds, Lego gave fans an early look at some of the pocket monsters that will be getting the brick-built treatment in 2027, revealing silhouettes of Grookey, Pichu, Mankey, Wingull and Charcadet. Beyond just which models builders will be able to piece together in the future, I had to ask about what’s to come from the Smart Brick.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtx1ttey00j23b66xjwwfnyf@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            As of now, Lego Pokémon only have a set amount of ways to interact with each other. But it may not be like that for long. Muthyala, with a large grin on his face, said he really wanted to share what was in the works, but couldn’t just yet. Andersen, on the other hand, provided some concrete insight into the future:
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtx2apdo00kx3b66r5s1z0xl@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            So while we have a confirmation that there’s more to come from the <a href="https://www.amazon.com/stores/page/1D1AD182-431E-4D34-9B76-749EBBB2B1CF?ingress=2&lp_context_asin=B0G2T1NQMW&visitId=64aa4366-22fd-4c43-846a-40758cff07cc&store_ref=bl_ast_dp_brandlogo_sto&ref_=ast_bln&tag=Underscoreddefault-20&ascsubtag=091126productlaunches" rel="nofollow sponsored" target="_blank">actual sets</a> in the Lego Smart Play collection, we’ll have to wait and see what the interactive elements of those builds look like. Back when I took a hands-on look at the Star Wars Smart Play sets, it felt like they weren’t fully taking advantage of the impressive technology inside of the Smart Brick. My time with the Pokémon sets is such a step forward in unlocking the full potential, and both Muthyala and Anderson seem excited to continue driving that forward.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtx2en2500l03b661greev5x@published"
        data-editable="text"

        data-article-gutter="true"

<h3

        The first gimbal camera with 4K vertical recording

  <div

            <div class="media__metadata-wrapper">
                <div class="interactive-video__metadata">
                    <div itemprop="caption" class="interactive-video__caption">
                        <span data-editable="metaCaption" class="inline-placeholder"></span>
                        <figcaption class="interactive-video__credit">Rikka Altland/CNN Underscored</figcaption>

</div>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtvo0yiw00023b66kmn5rvjb@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            Insta360 just launched its newest gimbal camera, the Luna Pro. Despite costing less than the <a href="https://www.amazon.com/Insta360-Luna-Ultra-Touchscreen-Photography-Cosmic/dp/B0GXJRJ2MK/?tag=Underscoreddefault-20&ascsubtag=091126productlaunches" rel="nofollow sponsored" target="_blank">Luna Ultra</a> that I’ve been using over the past few months, this is hardly a downgrade. In fact, it upgrades one key feature that even the higher-end version lacks; the ability to record 4K vertical video.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtvvv2j2000t3b66prwbk74n@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            Typically with these gimbal cameras, whether from Insta360 or DJI or some other brand, you’re limited to filming vertical content at 3K. Some of these video cameras are able to capture the world around you with an 8K resolution in landscape orientation. But when you want to record footage fit for sharing on Instagram or the social media platform of your choice? It’s locked to a lower quality. That’s no longer the case thanks to the debut of the Insta360 Luna Pro. Instead of hiding this feature behind a higher-end version, Insta360 has decided to release a more affordable iteration that improves one of the biggest use cases for this type of camera while making some sacrifices in other, less used areas. Filming 4K content in a portrait orientation will be rolling out to the Luna Ultra in the near future, but for now, it’s nice to see the cheaper model debut with such a highly sought-after feature.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtvw3k1k001f3b660abp0wm8@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            Aside from its vertical video capabilities, the biggest difference between the new Luna Pro and the Luna Ultra that came before it is the lack of a secondary sensor. The latter has a telephoto zoom lens that helps with taking videos of far away subjects, and for this new and more affordable version, Insta360 has ditched that feature. In my own personal testing, I haven’t found myself using the extra zoom capabilities all that much and certainly agree that it’s worth nixing from the experience in favor of saving nearly $200.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtvxpqm3000h3b66wmju1arg@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            Aside from the different camera array that rests on the gimbal, the Insta360 Luna Pro is every bit the same that I’ve been relying on for the past few months. It still includes the detachable screen and control pad that’s every bit as innovative on the new release as they are on the Ultra version. It still has solid battery life that can easily record clips throughout an entire day of on-and-off shooting. It still uses Leica color science for cinematic shots right out of the camera. And most importantly, its gimbal stabilization ensures that shaky videos are a thing of the past, even when you’re being nudged by waves while at the beach. All of that makes the <a href="https://www.amazon.com/Insta360-CINSACHA-Luna-Vlogging-Camera/dp/B0GY87RFYK?tag=Underscoreddefault-20&ascsubtag=091126productlaunches" rel="nofollow sponsored" target="_blank">lower $600 price tag</a> such a bargain in my book. Most casual videographers won’t miss any of the exclusive features that are only found on the Luna Ultra, especially with it landing at $170 below that higher-end version of the gimbal camera.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtn7t5fj007s27qhep263pv8@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            Whoop is the king of screen-free <a href="https://www.cnn.com/cnn-underscored/reviews/best-fitness-tracker">fitness trackers</a>. If you want a device that tracks your steps, heart rate and sleep without having to deal with a full smartwatch, Whoop truly is the device to dethrone. Earlier this year, the new <a href="https://www.cnn.com/cnn-underscored/reviews/google-fitbit-air">Fitbit Air</a> launched with a robust suite of health-tracking tech to help it take on such a worthy adversary, and now, it’s getting some extra help from an unlikely ally: Pikachu.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtvzhyaa002i3b66nohjnkk8@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            The new <a href="https://go.skimresources.com/?id=87732X1565017&url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.google.com%2Fconfig%2Fgoogle_fitbit_air%3Fhl%3Den-US%26selections%3DeyJwcm9kdWN0RmFtaWx5IjoiWjI5dloyeGxYMlpwZEdKcGRGOWhhWEk9IiwidmFyaWFudHMiOltbIjciLCJNVEk9Il0sWyIyIiwiT0E9PSJdXX0%253D&xcust=091126productlaunches" rel="nofollow sponsored" target="_blank">Pokémon Sleep edition</a> of the Fitbit Air is every bit the same health monitor that that my colleague and CNN Underscored’s senior testing editor, <a href="https://www.cnn.com/cnn-underscored/about/rick-stella">Rick Stella</a>, tried for himself <a href="https://www.cnn.com/cnn-underscored/reviews/google-fitbit-air">back in June</a>. It still handles keeping tabs on your well-being, works for up to seven days before needing to be recharged, can tag along in the shower and even while swimming with water-resistance that is rated to withstand depths of up to 50 meters.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtvzxxye00303b66mbcp36tf@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            It just has a fun new design that complements some added software tricks that allow the Fitbit Air to work with the smartphone app, Pokémon Sleep. Normally, you need to pay for a Google Health subscription in order to unlock deeper insight into your sleep routine and workout regimen. While Pokémon Sleep can’t help with the latter, it does unlock all kinds of info on how long and how well you sleep at night. It also adds some extra encouragement to getting to bed on time, with a simply delightful experience that turns catching some Zzz’s into catching Pokémon.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtvzhutc002g3b664k150v0e@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            During my time at the Pokémon World Championships, I also had a chance to check out the new wearable and put it to the test alongside the Pokémon Sleep app that I’ve used intermittently over the years. The Fitbit Air itself is such a simple yet great piece of hardware that truly lives up to the notion that you can just set it and forget it on your wrist. I may not be ditching my beloved Apple Watch anytime soon, but I do envy just how convenient it is to wear this screen-free fitness tracker. The newfound compatibility with the Pocket Monster-themed application is also a delight, and is a perfect match for the themed accessory. I can’t help being a bit biased that the Fitbit Air’s nylon strap has received a makeover to my favorite color, blue, and the little Pikachu insignia is just such a cute addition.
    </p>

            There’s a new contender for the best high-end mop, and it’s not from the usual suspects. Sure, Philips is no stranger to reliable appliances and gadgets that clean everything from floors to teeth, but its newest electric mop, <a href="https://go.skimresources.com/?id=87732X1565017&url=https%3A%2F%2Fus.home-appliances.philips%2Fproducts%2Fphilips-oneup-5000-series-cordless-electric-mop&xcust=091126productlaunches" rel="nofollow sponsored" target="_blank">the OneUp 5000</a>, takes that up a notch with a far more premium experience than the affordable options our editors typically recommend all at a fraction of the cost of other comparable solutions from Dyson, iRobot or Roborock.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtwynlcb00bq3b66ess7jn0d@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            The Philips OneUp 5000 rests somewhere between those feature-packed options and <a href="https://www.cnn.com/cnn-underscored/reviews/best-mops">traditional mops</a> like models from O-Cedar or Swiffer. Unlike the latter which keep clean by spreading dirty water around or relying on some kind of extra cleaning solution, the OneUp continuously pumps clean water onto your floor while simultaneously sucking in dirty water into a separate tank. It’s still quite the lightweight appliance, too, despite a pair of onboard water tanks and a rechargeable battery that powers the mopping experience for up to 70 minutes on a single charge. One of my favorite elements about the mop is that you won’t have to worry about wasting single-use cleaning pads that you’ll have to repurchase every few months. Instead, the OneUp relies on a reusable, machine-washable pad to do the job.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtw0rwta005g3b666ro5j2tj@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            I may be one of the biggest laptop trackpad fans around, but even I can’t ignore the siren song of a comfortable, ergonomic mouse. I’ve tried dozens over the years, and sadly, I almost always go back to using my trusty Apple Magic Trackpad. That streak was finally broken by the recent <a href="https://www.cnn.com/cnn-underscored/reviews/logitech-mx-master-4-mouse">Logitech MX Master 4</a>, a computer accessory that currently holds CNN Underscored’s title for the <a href="https://www.cnn.com/cnn-underscored/reviews/best-computer-mice">best mouse we’ve tested</a>. As much as I enjoy how comfortable it is to use for hours on end, it largely only ever lives on my desk. That’s all well and good for the days when I work in my home office, but if I find myself working by the window in my cozy lounge chair or even heading out to work at a coffee shop, I simply go back to using the trackpad built right into my laptop.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtw0vnm600613b66ny95rkyp@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            That’s where the <a href="https://go.shopyourlikes.com/pi/8fc5a4d4115d0aed49ede02c236c9a31bd8ba975?afId=728330&afCreativeId=2993&afPlacementId=091126productlaunches" rel="nofollow sponsored" target="_blank">new BenQ Inftylab M</a> comes into play. It’s one of the first ergonomic mice on the market that is designed specifically for Mac gestures, taking a more focused approach than the universal Mac and Windows compatibility that you’ll find from Logitech. Compared to the <a href="https://www.cnn.com/cnn-underscored/reviews/logitech-mx-master-4-mouse">MX Master 4</a>, the M Mouse is just shy of half its weight at just 85 grams. That’s really where BenQ’s newest mouse catches my attention. It may not cradle my hand in quite the same way as Logitech’s much larger and heavier peripheral, but the Inftylab M still feels great to use after a day of clicking and scrolling. Being able to bring the trackpad experience with me without wasting precious space in my backpack makes for an easy selling point, although the $100 price tag for this new mouse does make it a tougher comparison.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtw14eia006z3b664y305ydb@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            I’ll be excited to spend more time with the Inftylab mouse to see how it compares in the long run, but so far, I’m impressed by its ability to replicate trackpad and Multi-Touch gestures with its shortcut buttons on the side. Paired with its lightweight and ergonomic design, this is certainly a winning combination — especially if the larger Logitech MX options just aren’t as comfortable for those with smaller hands or practical to use while away from your home office. The BenQ Inftylab M Wireless Mouse is now available for preorder at retailers like <a href="https://go.shopyourlikes.com/pi/8fc5a4d4115d0aed49ede02c236c9a31bd8ba975?afId=728330&afCreativeId=2993&afPlacementId=091126productlaunches" rel="nofollow sponsored" target="_blank">B&H Photo Video for $100</a>.
    </p>

        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtwz874g00ds3b66jfl9m16i@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            Last up on the docket of new iPhone 18 cases are the <a href="https://www.dpbolvw.net/click-8314883-16959086?url=https%3A%2F%2Farc.cc%2Fproducts%2Farc-pulse-for-iphone-18-pro-max&sid=091126productlaunches" rel="nofollow sponsored" target="_blank">latest covers from Arc</a>. The brand takes a vastly different approach to protecting your new smartphone compared to any other accessories covered this week. That’s thanks to an aluminum build that aims to offer the most protection possible while also covering as little of your smartphone as it can. Each bumper case is made from two individual pieces of aluminum, which pair with rubber padding to protect the top and bottom corners of your handset. Arc Pulse cases lift your smartphone off a desk, so laying it down doesn’t scuff or scratch the screen.
    </p>

    <p
        class="paragraph inline-placeholder vossi-paragraph"
        data-uri="cms.cnn.com/_components/paragraph/instances/cmtwz87ul00du3b66x4b1cf3f@published"
        data-editable="text"
        data-component-name="paragraph"
        
        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            I have been a massive fan of these Arc bumper cases for years. There have been entire years where the only case I actually use with my annual iPhone upgrade is one of these Arc covers, and every time, I am always left impressed by how well something so minimal can actually protect my device. So, if you’re worried that these minimal covers don’t provide enough protection, hopefully my anecdotal experience with the accessory should help put your mind at ease. Alongside the refreshed designs fit for Apple’s newest Pro series smartphones (the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max), Arc is also shipping in six styles: Matte Black, Silver, Graphite, Rose Bronze, Gold and Titanium Onyx Black. Pricing across the new collection <a href="https://www.dpbolvw.net/click-8314883-16959086?url=https%3A%2F%2Farc.cc%2Fproducts%2Farc-pulse-for-iphone-18-pro-max&sid=091126productlaunches" rel="nofollow sponsored" target="_blank">starts at $70</a>.
    </p>

    <p

        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            As deals editors at CNN Underscored, we are some of the first people to hear about the latest product news from reader-favorite brands. That means our senior deals editor, <a href="https://www.cnn.com/cnn-underscored/about/rikka-altland">Rikka Altland</a>, follows a product from the moment it’s announced through testing it herself and then circling back once it begins going on sale.

        data-article-gutter="true"
    >
            Our goal here is to save you money, and by considering the entire journey of a product, we can offer better thoughts on if it’s worth your cash. .cnn-tooltip {
  position: relative;
}

.cnn-tooltip__blurb {
  background-color: #181d28;
  color: #fff;
  font-family: cnn_sans_display, helveticaneue, Helvetica, Arial, Utkal, sans-serif;
  font-weight: 400;
  font-size: 12px;
  line-height: 16px;
  border-radius: 5px;
  margin-top: 8px;
  text-align: left;
  max-width: 285px;
  z-index: 200;
  visibility: visible;
  opacity: 1;
  transition: visibility 0s, opacity 0.5s linear;
  position: absolute;
  width: max-content;
  padding: 16px 12px;
  right: -20px;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: row;
  align-items: flex-start;
}

.cnn-tooltip__blurb-text--emphasis {
  font-weight: 700;
}

.cnn-tooltip__blurb-text {
  width: 100%;
  margin: 0;
}

.cnn-tooltip__blurb-text::after {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  top: -20px;
  right: 8%;
  border-width: 10px;
  border-style: solid;
  border-color: transparent transparent #181d28 transparent;
}

.cnn-tooltip__close-btn {
  background-color: transparent;
  outline: none;
  border: none;
}

.cnn-tooltip__close-btn::before {
  content: '';
  -webkit-mask: url('/media/sites/cnn/icons/ui-close.svg');
  -webkit-mask-size: cover;
  background-color: #fff;
  outline: none;
  height: 16px;
  width: 16px;
  display: inline-block;
  cursor: pointer;
}

.cnn-tooltip--hidden .cnn-tooltip__blurb {
  visibility: hidden;
  opacity: 0;
}

.cnn-tooltip--centered .cnn-tooltip__blurb {
  right: unset;
  left: -50%;
}

.cnn-tooltip--centered .cnn-tooltip__blurb-text::after {
  left: 50%;
  right: unset;
}

.cnn-tooltip--above .cnn-tooltip__blurb-text::after {
  bottom: -20%;
  top: unset;
  border-color: #181d28 transparent transparent transparent;
}

.cnn-tooltip--above .cnn-tooltip__blurb {
  margin-top: 0;
  bottom: 125%;
}

.cnn-tooltip--left .cnn-tooltip__blurb {
  left: 0;
  margin-top:14px;
}

.cnn-tooltip--left .cnn-tooltip__blurb-text::after {
  left: 1%;
  right: unset;
}

@media screen and (min-width: 960px) {
  .cnn-tooltip--follow-mobile {
    display: none;
  }

  .cnn-tooltip--follow-desktop .cnn-tooltip__blurb {
    right: -18px;
    top: 38px;
  }

  .cnn-tooltip:has([aria-expanded="true"]) .tooltip__blurb {
    visibility: hidden;
    opacity: 0;
  }
}


@media screen and (max-width: 960px) {
  .header--active .cnn-tooltip__blurb {
    visibility: hidden;
    opacity: 0;
  }
}
